Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. import SystemE
import Book1.Prop10.Main
import Book1Variants.Prop23

namespace Elements.Book3

open Elements.Book1

-- orchestrator-agreed: construction — a given segment (3 non-collinear points: chord AC + arc point b) → ∃ the completed
-- circle through all three. Clean, proof-faithful (proof exhibits center, [3.9] completes; final sentence = the ∃).
theorem proposition_25 : ∀ (a b c : Point) (AC : Line),
  a.onLine AC ∧ c.onLine AC ∧ a ≠ c ∧ ¬b.onLine AC ∧ |(a─b)| = |(c─b)| →
  ∃ (α : Circle), a.onCircle α ∧ b.onCircle α ∧ c.onCircle α :=
by
  euclid_intros
  euclid_intro_sentence "3.25.0"
    "For a given segment of a circle, to complete the circle, the very one of which it is a segment. Let $ABC$ be the given segment of a circle. So it is required to complete the circle for segment $ABC$, the very one of which it is a segment."

  euclid_apply (proposition_10 a c AC) as d
  euclid_apply (line_from_points d b) as DB
  euclid_apply (line_from_points a b) as AB

  euclid_sentence "3.25.1"
    "For let $AC$ be cut in half at (point) $D$ [Prop.~1.10],"
    (step1 : between a d c ∧ |(a─d)| = |(d─c)|) := by sorry

  euclid_sentence "3.25.2"
    "and let $DB$ be drawn from point $D$, at right-angles to $AC$ [Prop.~1.11]."
    (step2 : ∠ a:d:b = ∟) := by sorry

  euclid_sentence "3.25.3"
    "And let $AB$ be joined."
    (step3 : distinctPointsOnLine a b AB) := by sorry

  euclid_sentence "3.25.4"
    "Thus, angle $ABD$ is surely either greater than, equal to, or less than (angle) $BAD$."
    (step4 : ∠ a:b:d > ∠ b:a:d ∨ ∠ a:b:d = ∠ b:a:d ∨ ∠ a:b:d < ∠ b:a:d) := by sorry

  by_cases hgt : ∠ a:b:d > ∠ b:a:d
  ·
    euclid_sentence "3.25.5"
      "First of all, let it be greater."
      (step5 : ∠ a:b:d > ∠ b:a:d) := by sorry

    euclid_apply (proposition_23' a b b a d d AB AB DB) as g
    euclid_apply (line_from_points a g) as AG
    have hAGDB : AG.intersectsLine DB := by sorry
    euclid_apply (intersection_lines AG DB) as e
    have hec : e ≠ c := by sorry
    euclid_apply (line_from_points e c) as EC
    euclid_apply (circle_from_points e a) as α₁

    euclid_sentence "3.25.6"
      "And let (angle) $BAE$, equal to angle $ABD$, be constructed on the straight-line $BA$, at the point $A$ on it [Prop.~1.23]."
      (step6 : ∠ b:a:e = ∠ a:b:d ∧ e ≠ a) := by sorry

    euclid_sentence "3.25.7"
      "And let $DB$ be drawn through to $E$,"
      (step7 : e.onLine DB) := by sorry

    euclid_sentence "3.25.8"

    euclid_sentence "3.25.11"

      (step11 : ∠ a:d:e = ∠ c:d:e) := by sorry

      "Thus, the base $AE$ is equal to the base $CE$ [Prop.~1.4]."
      (step12 : |(a─e)| = |(c─e)|) := by sorry

      (step15 : |(a─e)| = |(e─b)| ∧ |(e─b)| = |(e─c)|) := by sorry

    euclid_sentence "3.25.16"
      "Thus, if a circle is drawn with center $E$, and radius one of $AE$, $EB$, or $EC$, it will also go through the remaining points (of the segment), and the (associated circle) will be completed [Prop.~3.9]."

      (step18 : e.opposingSides b AC) := by sorry

      -- @assumption_valid

      euclid_sentence "3.25.19"
        "[And], similarly, even if angle $ABD$ is equal to $BAD$, (since) $AD$ becomes equal to each of $BD$ [Prop.~1.6] and $DC$, the three (straight-lines) $DA$, $DB$, and $DC$ will be equal to one another."
        (step19 : |(d─a)| = |(d─b)| ∧ |(d─b)| = |(d─c)|) := by sorry

      have hda : d ≠ a := by sorry

      euclid_sentence "3.25.21"
        "And $ABC$ will manifestly be a semi-circle."

      have hAG3DB : AG3.intersectsLine DB := by sorry

      euclid_apply (circle_from_points e a) as α₃

      -- @assumption ("$ABD$ is less than $BAD$", ∠ a:b:d < ∠ b:a:d)
      euclid_sentence "3.25.22"
        "And if $ABD$ is less than $BAD$, and we construct (angle $BAE$), equal to angle $ABD$, on the straight-line $BA$, at the point $A$ on it [Prop.~1.23], then the center will fall on $DB$, inside the segment $ABC$."
        (step22 : e.onLine DB ∧ e.sameSide b AC) := by sorry

      -- greater than semicircle: center E inside the chord AC's arc side
      euclid_sentence "3.25.23"
        "And segment $ABC$ will manifestly be greater than a semi-circle."
        (step23 : b.sameSide e AC) := by sorry

      have hEb : |(e─a)| = |(e─b)| := by sorry
      have hEc : |(e─a)| = |(e─c)| := by sorry
      use α₃
      have haα₃ : a.onCircle α₃ := by sorry
      have hbα₃ : b.onCircle α₃ := by sorry
      have hcα₃ : c.onCircle α₃ := by sorry
      exact ⟨haα₃, hbα₃, hcα₃⟩

  euclid_conclude_sentence "3.25.24"
    "Thus, a circle has been completed from the given segment of a circle. (Which is) the very thing it was required to do."

end Elements.Book3

import SystemE
import Book3.Prop06.step1
import Book3.Prop06.step2
import Book3.Prop06.step3
import Book3.Prop06.step4
import Book3.Prop06.step5
import Book3.Prop06.step6
import Book3.Prop06.step7
import Book3.Prop06.step8

namespace Elements.Book3

theorem proposition_6 : ∀ (ABC CDE : Circle),
  -- "touch" = Def III.3 (meet but do not cut), NOT "exactly one point" (that is the later theorem
  -- III.13, which cites III.11 — defining touch as ∃! here would be circular). `ABC ≠ CDE` is the
  -- "two distinct circles" of the enunciation (same-circle satisfies meet+don't-cut, so it's needed).
  ABC ≠ CDE →
  (∃ c : Point, c.onCircle ABC ∧ c.onCircle CDE) ∧ ¬ ABC.intersectsCircle CDE →
  ¬ ∃ f : Point, f.isCentre ABC ∧ f.isCentre CDE :=
by
  euclid_intros

  euclid_intro_sentence "3.6.0"
    "If two circles touch one another, (then) they will not have the same center. For let the two circles $ABC$ and $CDE$ touch one another at point $C$. I say that they will not have the same center."
  obtain ⟨c, hcABC, hcCDE⟩ := left

  have habsurd1 : ¬(∃ f : Point, f.isCentre ABC ∧ f.isCentre CDE) := by
    intro hsuppose1
    obtain ⟨f, hfABC, hfCDE⟩ := hsuppose1
    euclid_sentence "3.6.1"
      "For, if possible, let $F$ be (the common center),"
      (step1 : f.isCentre ABC ∧ f.isCentre CDE) := by
        euclid_apply (helper_3_6_step1 f ABC CDE
          (by euclid_assumption "" (show f.isCentre ABC; assumption))
          (by euclid_assumption "" (show f.isCentre CDE; assumption)))

    euclid_apply (line_from_points f c) as FC
    euclid_sentence "3.6.2"
      "and let $FC$ be joined,"
      (step2 : f.onLine FC ∧ c.onLine FC) := by
        euclid_apply (helper_3_6_step2 f c FC
          (by euclid_assumption "" (show f.onLine FC; assumption))
          (by euclid_assumption "" (show c.onLine FC; assumption)))

    -- Draw a line FEB through f (the supposed centre): b a point on ABC, FEB = line f b,
    -- which meets CDE (f is interior to CDE) at e.
    euclid_apply (exists_point_on_circle ABC) as b
    euclid_apply (line_from_points f b) as FEB
    have hFEB_int : FEB.intersectsCircle CDE := by euclid_finish
    euclid_apply (intersections_circle_line CDE FEB) as (e, e2)
    euclid_sentence "3.6.3"
      "and let $FEB$ be drawn through (the two circles), at random."
      (step3 : b.onCircle ABC ∧ e.onCircle CDE ∧
               f.onLine FEB ∧ e.onLine FEB ∧ b.onLine FEB) := by
        euclid_apply (helper_3_6_step3 b e f ABC CDE FEB
          (by euclid_assumption "" (show b.onCircle ABC; assumption))
          (by euclid_assumption "" (show e.onCircle CDE; assumption))
          (by euclid_assumption "" (show f.onLine FEB; assumption))
          (by euclid_assumption "" (show e.onLine FEB; assumption))
          (by euclid_assumption "" (show b.onLine FEB; assumption)))

    -- @assumption_valid
    have step4_assumption1 : f.isCentre ABC := by assumption
    -- @assumption ("point $F$ is the center of the circle $ABC$", f.isCentre ABC)
    euclid_sentence "3.6.4"
      "Therefore, since point $F$ is the center of the circle $ABC$, $FC$ is equal to $FB$."
      (step4 : |(f─c)| = |(f─b)|) := by
        euclid_apply (helper_3_6_step4 f c b ABC
          (by euclid_assumption "point $F$ is the center of the circle $ABC$" (show f.isCentre ABC; assumption))
          (by euclid_assumption "" (show c.onCircle ABC; assumption))
          (by euclid_assumption "" (show b.onCircle ABC; assumption)))

    -- @assumption_valid
    have step5_assumption1 : f.isCentre CDE := by assumption
    -- @assumption ("point $F$ is the center of the circle $CDE$", f.isCentre CDE)
    euclid_sentence "3.6.5"
      "Again, since point $F$ is the center of the circle $CDE$, $FC$ is equal to $FE$."
      (step5 : |(f─c)| = |(f─e)|) := by
        euclid_apply (helper_3_6_step5 f c e CDE
          (by euclid_assumption "point $F$ is the center of the circle $CDE$" (show f.isCentre CDE; assumption))
          (by euclid_assumption "" (show c.onCircle CDE; assumption))
          (by euclid_assumption "" (show e.onCircle CDE; assumption)))

    -- @assumption_valid
    have step6_assumption1 : |(f─c)| = |(f─b)| := by assumption
    -- @assumption ("$FC$ was shown (to be) equal to $FB$", |(f─c)| = |(f─b)|)
    euclid_sentence "3.6.6"
      "But $FC$ was shown (to be) equal to $FB$. Thus, $FE$ is also equal to $FB$, the lesser to the greater."
      (step6 : |(f─e)| = |(f─b)|) := by
        euclid_apply (helper_3_6_step6 f c e b
          (by euclid_assumption "$FC$ was shown (to be) equal to $FB$" (show |(f─c)| = |(f─b)|; assumption))
          (by euclid_assumption "" (show |(f─c)| = |(f─e)|; assumption)))

    euclid_sentence "3.6.7"
      "The very thing is impossible."
      (step7 : False) := by
        euclid_apply (helper_3_6_step7 f e b ABC CDE
          (by euclid_assumption "" (show |(f─e)| = |(f─b)|; assumption))
          (by euclid_assumption "" (show f.isCentre CDE; assumption))
          (by euclid_assumption "" (show f.isCentre ABC; assumption))
          (by euclid_assumption "" (show e.onCircle CDE; assumption))
          (by euclid_assumption "" (show b.onCircle ABC; assumption))
          (by euclid_assumption "" (show ABC ≠ CDE; assumption)))
    exact step7

  euclid_sentence "3.6.8"
    "Thus, point $F$ is not the (common) center of the circles $ABC$ and $CDE$."
    (step8 : ¬(∃ f : Point, f.isCentre ABC ∧ f.isCentre CDE)) := by
      euclid_apply (helper_3_6_step8 ABC CDE
        (by euclid_assumption "" (show ¬(∃ f : Point, f.isCentre ABC ∧ f.isCentre CDE); assumption)))
  -- step8 : ¬∃f,... applied to the telescoped reductio hyp (a✝) closes the False goal
  exact step8 ‹∃ f : Point, f.isCentre ABC ∧ f.isCentre CDE›
  euclid_conclude_sentence "3.6.9"
    "Thus, if two circles touch one another, (then) they will not have the same center. (Which is) the very thing it was required to show."

end Elements.Book3

import SystemE
import Book1.Prop08.Main
import Book1.Prop20.Main
import Book1Variants.Prop22
import Book1.Prop23.Main

namespace Elements.Book1

theorem proposition_23' : ∀ (a b c d e x : Point) (AB CD CE : Line),
  distinctPointsOnLine a b AB ∧ formRectilinearAngle d c e CD CE ∧ ¬(x.onLine AB) →
  ∃ f : Point, f ≠ a ∧ (f.onLine AB ∨ f.sameSide x AB) ∧ (∠ f:a:b = ∠ d:c:e) :=
by
  euclid_intros
  by_cases (d.onLine CE)
  . -- Omitted by Euclid.
    by_cases (∠ d:c:e = 0)
    . use b
      euclid_finish
    . euclid_assert ∠ d:c:e = ∟ + ∟
      euclid_apply (extend_point AB b a) as b'
      use b'
      euclid_finish
  euclid_apply (line_from_points d e) as DE
  -- Euclid didn't explicitly apply proposition_20.
  euclid_apply (proposition_20 c d e CD DE CE)
  euclid_apply (proposition_20 d e c DE CE CD)
  euclid_apply (proposition_20 e c d CE CD DE)
  euclid_apply (proposition_22'' c d c e e d a b x CD CE DE AB) as (f, g)
  euclid_apply (line_from_points a f) as AF
  euclid_apply (line_from_points f g) as FG
  euclid_apply (proposition_8 c d e a f g CD DE CE AF FG AB)
  use f
  euclid_finish

end Elements.Book1

import SystemE

namespace Elements.Book1

theorem proposition_4 : ∀ (a b c d e f : Point) (AB BC AC DE EF DF : Line),
  formTriangle a b c AB BC AC ∧ formTriangle d e f DE EF DF ∧
  |(a─b)| = |(d─e)| ∧ |(a─c)| = |(d─f)| ∧ (∠ b:a:c = ∠ e:d:f) →
  |(b─c)| = |(e─f)| ∧ (∠ a:b:c = ∠ d:e:f) ∧ (∠ a:c:b = ∠ d:f:e) := by
  euclid_intros
  euclid_intro_sentence "1.4.0"
    "If two triangles have two  sides equal to two sides, respectively, and have the angle(s) enclosed by the equal straight-lines equal, then they will also have the base equal to the base, and the triangle will be equal to the triangle,  and the remaining angles subtended by the equal sides will be equal to the corresponding remaining angles. Let $ABC$ and $DEF$ be  two triangles having the two sides $AB$ and $AC$ equal to the two sides $DE$ and $DF$, respectively. (That is) $AB$ to $DE$, and $AC$ to $DF$. And (let) the angle $BAC$ (be) equal to the angle $EDF$. I say that the base $BC$ is also equal to the base $EF$, and  triangle $ABC$ will be equal to triangle $DEF$, and the remaining angles subtended by the equal sides will be equal to the corresponding remaining angles. (That is) $ABC$ to $DEF$, and $ACB$ to $DFE$."

  -- Superposition = "apply △ABC onto △DEF": apex A placed on D, AB laid on DE.
  -- Outputs: b' = image of B, c' = image of C, BC' = image line of BC, DC' = image line of AC.
  euclid_apply (superposition a b c d e f AB BC AC DE) as (b', c', BC', DC')
  -- ptImg: the superposition map — a↦d (apex placed on D), b↦b', c↦c'.
  classical
  let ptImg : Point → Point := fun p =>
    if p = a then d else
    if p = b then b' else
    if p = c then c' else
    p

  let lineImg : Line → Line := fun L =>
    if L = AB then DE else
    if L = AC then DC' else
    if L = BC then BC' else
    L

  have h_ptImg_a : ptImg a = d := by simp (config := { zetaDelta := true })
  have h_ptImg_b : ptImg b = b' := by simp (config := { zetaDelta := true }) [Ne.symm right_3]
  have h_ptImg_c : ptImg c = c' := by
    have hca : c ≠ a := fun h => left_7 (two_points_determine_line b c AB BC
      ⟨⟨left_3, by rw [h]; assumption, fun heq => right_3 (heq.trans h).symm⟩, left_2, left_4⟩)
    have hcb : c ≠ b := fun h => right_8 (two_points_determine_line a c AB AC
      ⟨⟨by assumption, by rw [h]; assumption, fun heq => right_3 (heq.trans h)⟩, left_6, left_5⟩).symm
    simp (config := { zetaDelta := true }) [hca, hcb]
  have h_lineImg_AB : lineImg AB = DE := by simp (config := { zetaDelta := true })
  have h_lineImg_AC : lineImg AC = DC' := by simp (config := { zetaDelta := true }) [right_8]
  have h_lineImg_BC : lineImg BC = BC' := by

import SystemE.Theory.Relations

axiom line_from_points : ∀ (a b : Point), a ≠ b →
  ∃ L : Line, (a.onLine L) ∧ (b.onLine L)

axiom circle_from_points : ∀ (a b : Point), a ≠ b →
  ∃ α : Circle, (a.isCentre α) ∧ (b.onCircle α)
import SystemE.Theory.Constructions.Points

axiom intersection_lines : ∀ (L M : Line), L.intersectsLine M →
  ∃ a : Point, (a.onLine L) ∧ (a.onLine M)

theorem proposition_9 : ∀ (ABC : Circle) (a b c d : Point),
    d.insideCircle ABC ∧

import SystemE.Theory.Sorts

opaque Point.onLine : Point → Line → Prop

@[simp]
abbrev distinctPointsOnLine : Point → Point → Line → Prop := λ P Q L => P.onLine L ∧ Q.onLine L ∧ P ≠ Q

namespace Point

opaque sameSide : Point → Point → Line → Prop

@[simp]
abbrev opposingSides : Point → Point → Line → Prop :=
  λ a b l => ¬ a.onLine l  ∧ ¬ b.onLine l ∧ ¬ sameSide a b l

end Point

opaque collinear (a b c : Point) : Prop



/--
`between x y z` means `y` is between `x` and `z`
-/
opaque between : Point → Point → Point → Prop


namespace Point

opaque onCircle : Point → Circle → Prop

opaque insideCircle : Point → Circle → Prop

@[simp]
abbrev outsideCircle : Point → Circle → Prop :=
λ p c => ¬ p.insideCircle c ∧ ¬ p.onCircle c

opaque isCentre : Point → Circle → Prop

end Point

namespace Line

opaque intersectsLine : Line → Line → Prop

opaque intersectsCircle : Line → Circle → Prop


end Line

namespace Circle

opaque intersectsCircle : Circle → Circle → Prop

import SystemE.Theory.Sorts
import SystemE.Theory.Relations

--
-- Metric inferences defined in Sec. 3.5 of Avigad et al., 2009
-- Generally speaking, they are not used explicitly in the tactics written by humans.
-- *
--   + is associative and commutative, with identity 0.

--   < is a linear ordering with least element 0

--   For any x, y, and z, if x < y then x + z < y + z

--
-- 1.
-- ab = 0 if and only if a = b.
--



axiom zero_segment_if :
  ∀ (a b : Point),  |(a ─ b)| = 0 → a = b


axiom zero_segment_onlyif : ∀ (a b : Point),
  a = b → |(a─b)| = 0

-- --
-- 2.
-- ab ≥ 0
--
-- @[simp]
axiom segment_gte_zero : ∀ (s : Segment),
  0 ≤ s.length

--
-- 3.
-- ab = ba.
--
-- @[simp]
axiom segment_symmetric : ∀ (a b : Point),
  |(a─b)| = |(b─a)|
--


axiom angle_symm : ∀ (a b c : Point),
  (a ≠ b) ∧ (b ≠ c) → ((∠ a:b:c) = (∠ c:b:a))

--
-- 5.
-- 0 ≤ \abc and \abc ≤ right-angle + right-angle.
-- --
-- @[simp]
axiom angle_range : ∀ (ang : Angle),
  (0 : ℝ) ≤ ang ∧ ang ≤ ∟ + ∟

-- A right angle is a positive quantity. `∟` (Angle.Right) is an opaque real with no
-- built-in positivity, so without this the angle theory is satisfiable by ∟ = 0, which
-- collapses every "collinear points subtend a right angle ⟹ False" argument (the solver
-- sets ∟ = 0 and both degenerate branches — degenerated_angle giving 0 and flat_angle
-- giving ∟ + ∟ — close vacuously). Post. 4 fixes ∟ as a definite quantity, and Def. I.10
-- defines it by a non-degenerate geometric act (a line standing on another), both of which
-- entail ∟ > 0. A constraint on the opaque measurement constant, not a derivable claim.
axiom right_angle_pos : (0 : ℝ) < ∟

--
-- 6.
-- △aab = 0. △
--
-- @[simp]
axiom degenerated_area : ∀ (a b : Point), Triangle.area △ a:a:b = 0

--
-- 7.
-- △abc ≥ 0.
-- --
-- @[simp]
axiom area_gte_zero : ∀ (ar : Triangle), 0 ≤ Triangle.area ar

--
-- 8.
-- △abc = △cab and △abc = △acb.
--
-- @[simp]
axiom area_symm_1 : ∀ (a b c : Point),
    Triangle.area (△a:b:c) = Triangle.area (△c:a:b)

-- @[simp]
axiom area_symm_2 : ∀ (a b c : Point),
    Triangle.area (△ a:b:c) = Triangle.area (△a:c:b)

--
-- 9.
-- If ab = a′b′, bc = b′c′, ca = c′a′, \abc = \a′b′c′, \bca = \b′c′a′, and
-- \cab = \c′a′b′, then △abc = △a′b′c′.
--

axiom area_congruence : ∀ (a b c a' b' c' : Point),
    |(a─b)| = |(a'─b')| ∧
    |(b─c)| = |(b'─c')| ∧
    |(c─a)| = |(c'─a')| ∧
    ∠ a:b:c = ∠ a':b':c' ∧
    ∠ b:c:a = ∠ b':c':a' ∧
    ∠ c:a:b = ∠ c':a':b'
    → Triangle.area (△ a:b:c) = Triangle.area (△ a':b':c')

import SystemE.Theory.Sorts
import SystemE.Theory.Relations


--
-- Transfer inferences defined in Sec. 3.6 of Avigad et al. 2009
--
--    diagram-segment transfer axioms

--
-- 1.
-- If b is  between a and c, then ab + bc = ac.
-- [between_if, equal_circles, point_on_circle_if, point_on_circle_onlyif, sum_angles_if, sum_angles_onlyif, perpendicudlar_if, sum_areas_if]

-- Given any points a, b and c such that b is between a and c, then the straight-line from a to c is equal to the sum of the straight-lines from a to b and from b to c.
axiom between_if : ∀ (a b c : Point),
  between a b c → |(a─b)| + |(b─c)| = |(a─c)|

--
-- 2.
-- If a is the centre of α and β, b is on α, c is on β, and ab = ac, then α = β.


-- If a point x is the centre of two circles C and D, and given points b and d such that b is on C and c is on D and the straight-line from x to b is equal to the straight-line from x to c, then C is equal to D.
axiom equal_circles : ∀ (a b c : Point) (α β : Circle),
  (a.isCentre α) ∧ (a.isCentre β) ∧ (b.onCircle α) ∧ (c.onCircle β) ∧ |(a─b)| = |(a─c)| → α = β

--
-- 3.
-- If a is the centre of α and b is on α, then ac = ab if and only if c is on α.


-- If a point x is the centre of circle C and a point b is on C, then given some point c such that the straight-line from x to c is equal to the straight-line from x to b, then c is on C.
axiom point_on_circle_if : ∀ (a b c : Point) (α : Circle),
  (a.isCentre α) ∧ (b.onCircle α) ∧ |(a─c)| = |(a─b)| → c.onCircle α

@[aesop unsafe 80% [forward, apply]]
-- If a point x is the centre of circle C and a point b is on C, then given some point c on C, the straight-line from x to c is equal to the straight-line from x to b
axiom point_on_circle_onlyif : ∀ (a b c : Point) (α : Circle),
  (a.isCentre α) ∧ (b.onCircle α) ∧ (c.onCircle α) → |(a─c)| = |(a─b)|

--
-- 4.
-- If a is the centre of α and b is on α, and ac < ab if and only if c is in α.
--
-- -- Given any points b and c, and circle C, such that b is on C and the straight-line from the centre of C to c is less than the straight-line from the centre of C to b, then c is inside the circle C.
axiom point_in_circle_if : ∀ (a b c : Point) (α : Circle),
  (a.isCentre α) ∧ (b.onCircle α) ∧ |(a─c)| < |(a─b)| → c.insideCircle α

--
-- -- Given any points b and c, and circle C, such that b is on C and c is inside the circle C, then the straight-line from the centre of C to c is less than the straight-line from the centre of C to b.
axiom point_in_circle_onlyif : ∀ (a b c : Point) (α : Circle),
  (a.isCentre α) ∧ (b.onCircle α) ∧ (c.insideCircle α) → |(a─c)| < |(a─b)|

--    diagram-angle transfer axioms

--
-- 1.
-- Suppose a != b, a != c, a is on L, and b is on L. Then c is on L and a is
-- not  between b and c if and only if \bac = 0.
--
-- Given points a, b and c such that a is not equal to b and a is not equal to c, and line L such that a, b, and c are all on L, and a is not between b and c, then the angle bac has degree zero.
axiom degenerated_angle_if : ∀ (a b c : Point) (L : Line),
  (a ≠ b) ∧ (a ≠ c) ∧ (a.onLine L) ∧ (b.onLine L) ∧ (c.onLine L) ∧ ¬(between b a c) → ∠ b:a:c = 0

-- Given points a, b and c such that a is not equal to b and a is not equal to c, and line L such that a and b are on L, and the angle formed by b:a:c has degree zero,  then c is on L and a is not between b and c.
axiom degenerated_angle_onlyif : ∀ (a b c : Point) (L : Line),
  (a ≠ b) ∧ (a ≠ c) ∧ (a.onLine L) ∧ (b.onLine L) ∧ (∠ b:a:c = 0)  → (c.onLine L) ∧ ¬(between b a c)
--
-- -- Given points a, b and c such that a is not equal to b and a is not equal to c, and line L such that a and b are on L, and the angle formed by b:a:c has degree zero,  then c is on L and a is not between b and c.
-- axiom degenerated_angle_onlyif : ∀ (a b c : Point) (L : Line),
--   (a ≠ b) ∧ (a ≠ c) ∧ (a.onLine L) ∧ (b.onLine L) ∧ (∠ b: a: c) = (0 : ℝ) → (c.onLine L) ∧ ¬(between b a c)

-- --
-- 2.
-- Suppose a is on L and M, b is on L, c is on M, a != b, a != c, d is not on
-- L or M, and L != M. Then \bac = \bad + \dac if and only if b and d
-- are on the same side of M and c and d are on the same side of L.
--

-- Given point on a given lines L and M, point b  on L, and point c on M with a distinct from b, a distinct from c, point d  not on L or M, and L distinct from M, then the angle bac is equal to the sum of angles bad and dac only if b and d are on the same side of M and c and d are on the same side of L.

axiom sum_areas_onlyif : ∀ (a b c d : Point) (L : Line),
  (a.onLine L) ∧ (b.onLine L) ∧ (c.onLine L) ∧ (a ≠ b) ∧ (a ≠ c) ∧ (b ≠ c) ∧ ¬(d.onLine L) ∧
  (Triangle.area △ a:c:d + Triangle.area △ d:c:b = Triangle.area △ a:d:b) →
  between a c b

--    parallelogram rules

/--
Not in [Avigad et al., 2009]
-/
-- Given a parallelogram formed from points a, b, c and d, the sum of the areas of the triangles acd and adb is equal to the sum of the areas of triangles bac and bcd
axiom parallelogram_area : ∀ (a b c d : Point) (AB CD AC BD : Line), formParallelogram a b c d AB CD AC BD →
  Triangle.area △ a:c:d + Triangle.area △ a:d:b = Triangle.area △ b:a:c + Triangle.area △ b:c:d

-- /--
-- Not in [Avigad et al., 2009]
-- -/
--
-- Given a parallelogram formed from points a, b, c and d, and given points e and f such that e is betwen a and b and f is between c and d, then the sum of the areas of the triangles acf, afe, efd, and edb is equal to the sum of the areas of triangles acd and adb
axiom sum_parallelograms_area : ∀ (a b c d e f : Point) (AB CD AC BD : Line),
  formParallelogram a b c d AB CD AC BD ∧ between a e b ∧ between c f d →
  Triangle.area △ a:c:f + Triangle.area △ a:f:e + (Triangle.area △ e:f:d) + (Triangle.area △ e:d:b) = (Triangle.area △ a:c:d) + (Triangle.area △ a:d:b)


/--
Not in [Avigad et al., 2009] but required by Proposition 47
-/
axiom rectangle_area : ∀ (a b c d : Point) (AB CD AC BD : Line),
  formParallelogram a b c d AB CD AC BD ∧ (∠ a:c:d = ∟) →
  (Triangle.area △ a:c:d + Triangle.area △ a:b:d = |(a─b)| * |(a─c)|) ∧ (Triangle.area △ b:a:c + Triangle.area △ b:d:c) = |(a─b)| * |(a─c)|

4	# Faithfulness annotations (`euclid_sentence`)
5	
6	This module makes the Euclid → Lean *sentence mapping* a first-class proof object.
7	
8	A proof step that realizes one of Euclid's sentences is written with `euclid_sentence`
9	instead of a bare `have`.  It behaves exactly like `have name : type := by tac` (so the
10	proof term, local context and SMT query are unchanged) but additionally records, into a
11	persistent environment extension, the tuple
12	
13	    (locator, euclid-text, lean-type, have-name, source-position)
14	-/
15	
16	open Lean Elab Tactic Meta
17	
18	namespace SystemE.Tactics
19	
20	/-- One recorded faithfulness annotation: an Euclid sentence and the Lean step realizing it. -/
21	structure FaithfulEntry where
22	  /-- Source-anchored locator, e.g. `"2.1.8"` = Book 2, Prop 1, sentence 8. -/
23	  loc  : String
24	  /-- Euclid's verbatim sentence (the thing concatenation must recover). -/
25	  text : String
26	  /-- Surface syntax of the realizing step's type (for the human review table).
27	  Empty for `structural` entries, which emit no `have`. -/
28	  type : String
29	  /-- The `have` name introduced by the step, e.g. `"step8"`. Empty for `structural` entries. -/
30	  name : String
31	  /-- Source position `"line:col"` of the annotation. -/
32	  pos  : String
33	  /-- Module the annotation occurred in, e.g. `"Book2.Prop01"`. Used by the external checker to
34	  associate this sentence's block (same module) with `appliedExt` dependency entries. -/
35	  mod  : String
36	  /-- Source line of the annotation (integer; matches `appliedExt.line` for block association). -/
37	  line : Nat
38	  /-- `"logical"` = a real proof step (`euclid_sentence`, emits a `have`); `"structural"` =
39	  enunciation / "I say that" / QED boilerplate (`euclid_intro_sentence` /
40	  `euclid_conclude_sentence`) that contributes its text to the criterion-1 concatenation but is
41	  NOT a logical step — it attaches to `euclid_intros` / the final `exact` and emits no `have`. -/
42	  kind : String
43	  deriving Inhabited, Repr
44	
45	/-- Persistent env extension storing all `FaithfulEntry`s.  Entries from imported modules
46	are folded in, so a reader sees the current module plus its transitive imports.
47	(Shape follows Mathlib's `Mathlib/Tactic/Hint.lean`.) -/
48	initialize faithfulExt :
49	    SimplePersistentEnvExtension FaithfulEntry (List FaithfulEntry) ←
50	  registerSimplePersistentEnvExtension {
51	    addEntryFn := (·.cons)
52	    addImportedFn := mkStateFromImportedEntries (·.cons) {}
53	  }
54	
55	/-- Current annotation's location: `(pos "line:col", module string, line number)`. -/
56	private def refLoc : TacticM (String × String × Nat) := do
57	  let fileMap ← getFileMap
58	  let modName := (← getMainModule).toString
59	  return match (← getRef).getPos? with
60	    | some p => let lc := fileMap.toPosition p; (s!"{lc.line}:{lc.column}", modName, lc.line)
61	    | none   => ("?", modName, 0)
62	
63	/-- `euclid_sentence "loc" "euclid text" (name : type) := by tac`
64	
65	Realizes one Euclid sentence.  Elaborates to `have name : type := by tac` (identical proof
66	term / context to a plain `have`) and records a `logical` annotation into `faithfulExt`. -/
67	syntax (name := euclidSentence)
68	  "euclid_sentence " str str "(" ident " : " term ")" ":=" "by " tacticSeq : tactic
69	
70	elab_rules : tactic
71	  | `(tactic| euclid_sentence $loc:str $txt:str ($nm:ident : $ty:term) := by $tac) => do
72	    let (posStr, modName, lineNo) ← refLoc
73	    -- Surface syntax of the type (verbatim slice when available).
74	    let typeStr := (ty.raw.reprint).getD (toString ty)
75	    modifyEnv fun env => faithfulExt.addEntry env {
76	      loc  := loc.getString
77	      text := txt.getString
78	      type := typeStr
79	      name := nm.getId.toString
80	      pos  := posStr
81	      mod  := modName
82	      line := lineNo
83	      kind := "logical" }
84	    -- Emit the real `have`; proof term and local context unchanged.
85	    evalTactic (← `(tactic| have $nm:ident : $ty := by $tac))
86	
87	/-- `euclid_intro_sentence "loc" "euclid text"` and `euclid_conclude_sentence "loc" "euclid text"`
88	
89	Record a *structural* Euclid sentence — the enunciation / "I say that" preamble (placed right
90	after `euclid_intros`) or the closing restatement + QED boilerplate (placed at the final step).
91	These contribute their text to the criterion-1 concatenation but are NOT logical steps: they emit
92	no `have` (the tactic is a `skip`), so the proof term and local context are unchanged. -/
93	syntax (name := euclidIntroSentence)
94	  "euclid_intro_sentence " str str : tactic
95	syntax (name := euclidConcludeSentence)
96	  "euclid_conclude_sentence " str str : tactic
97	
98	/-- `euclid_wts "loc" "euclid text"`
99	
100	Record a *structural* mid-proof "I say that …" (what-to-show) sentence. Like the intro/conclude
101	tactics it emits no `have` (proof term / context unchanged) and only contributes its text to the
102	criterion-1 concatenation — but unlike them it is permitted MID-proof. Euclid's "I say that X"
103	announces the goal; it is NOT an assertion that X is already proven, so it carries no claim. The real
104	content X is established by the following sentences and assembled by the trailing `exact`. -/
105	syntax (name := euclidWts)
106	  "euclid_wts " str str : tactic
107	
108	/-- Shared recorder for the structural tactics. -/
109	private def recordStructural (loc txt : TSyntax `str) : TacticM Unit := do
110	  let (posStr, modName, lineNo) ← refLoc
111	  modifyEnv fun env => faithfulExt.addEntry env {
112	    loc  := loc.getString
113	    text := txt.getString
114	    type := ""
115	    name := ""
116	    pos  := posStr
117	    mod  := modName
118	    line := lineNo
119	    kind := "structural" }
120	  -- No tactic is emitted: this is a pure annotation, valid whether or not goals remain (it may
121	  -- follow the final `exact`). Recording only — proof term and local context are untouched.
122	  pure ()
123	
124	elab_rules : tactic
125	  | `(tactic| euclid_intro_sentence $loc:str $txt:str)    => recordStructural loc txt
126	  | `(tactic| euclid_conclude_sentence $loc:str $txt:str) => recordStructural loc txt
127	  | `(tactic| euclid_wts $loc:str $txt:str)               => recordStructural loc txt
128	
129	-- Faithfulness CHECKING (criterion 1: concatenate sentence texts, compare to the canonical
130	-- source) is done OUTSIDE Lean by `scripts/check_faithful.py`, which reads these annotations
131	-- from the source file. That keeps text-checking instant (no recompile / no SMT). This module
132	-- only RECORDS the annotations; the optional `lake exe` gate that reads them back from the
133	-- compiled .olean is deferred (see plan / todos).
134	
135	/-- `euclid_assumption "euclid text" (tac)` — every wired hypothesis slot, in ONE fixed shape.
136	
137	A string (documentary — Lean ignores it; the faithfulness checker reads it to confirm a reasoning
138	citation is a substring of its sentence) followed by a single **bracket-delimited** tactic that is the
139	actual proof. `wire_main.py` emits exactly:
140	
141	    (by euclid_assumption "TEXT" (show T; assumption))     -- structural (TEXT = "") and plain reasoning
142	    (by euclid_assumption "TEXT" (show T; exact pf))       -- reasoning whose input is a conjunct projection
143	
144	The brackets bound the proof unambiguously (so the recognizer's balanced-paren scan finds its end at any
145	depth, and Lean parses it as one parenthesized tactic); `show T` makes the slot's type visible and is
146	checked against the goal; the trailing tactic closes it from context. The text is `"`-free by
147	construction. There is no separate `use_override` syntax — an override is just `exact pf` inside the
148	brackets. -/
149	syntax (name := euclidAssumption)
150	  "euclid_assumption" str tactic : tactic
151	
152	elab_rules : tactic
153	  | `(tactic| euclid_assumption $_:str $t:tactic) => evalTactic t
154	
155	end SystemE.Tactics

import SystemE.Meta.Tactics.Solve

/-!
# Faithfulness annotations (`euclid_sentence`)

This module makes the Euclid → Lean *sentence mapping* a first-class proof object.

A proof step that realizes one of Euclid's sentences is written with `euclid_sentence`
instead of a bare `have`.  It behaves exactly like `have name : type := by tac` (so the
proof term, local context and SMT query are unchanged) but additionally records, into a
persistent environment extension, the tuple

    (locator, euclid-text, lean-type, have-name, source-position)
-/

open Lean Elab Tactic Meta

namespace SystemE.Tactics

/-- One recorded faithfulness annotation: an Euclid sentence and the Lean step realizing it. -/
structure FaithfulEntry where
  /-- Source-anchored locator, e.g. `"2.1.8"` = Book 2, Prop 1, sentence 8. -/
  loc  : String
  /-- Euclid's verbatim sentence (the thing concatenation must recover). -/
  text : String
  /-- Surface syntax of the realizing step's type (for the human review table).
  Empty for `structural` entries, which emit no `have`. -/
  type : String
  /-- The `have` name introduced by the step, e.g. `"step8"`. Empty for `structural` entries. -/
  name : String
  /-- Source position `"line:col"` of the annotation. -/
  pos  : String
  /-- Module the annotation occurred in, e.g. `"Book2.Prop01"`. Used by the external checker to
  associate this sentence's block (same module) with `appliedExt` dependency entries. -/
  mod  : String
  /-- Source line of the annotation (integer; matches `appliedExt.line` for block association). -/
  line : Nat
  /-- `"logical"` = a real proof step (`euclid_sentence`, emits a `have`); `"structural"` =
  enunciation / "I say that" / QED boilerplate (`euclid_intro_sentence` /
  `euclid_conclude_sentence`) that contributes its text to the criterion-1 concatenation but is
  NOT a logical step — it attaches to `euclid_intros` / the final `exact` and emits no `have`. -/
  kind : String
  deriving Inhabited, Repr

/-- Persistent env extension storing all `FaithfulEntry`s.  Entries from imported modules
are folded in, so a reader sees the current module plus its transitive imports.
(Shape follows Mathlib's `Mathlib/Tactic/Hint.lean`.) -/
initialize faithfulExt :
    SimplePersistentEnvExtension FaithfulEntry (List FaithfulEntry) ←
  registerSimplePersistentEnvExtension {
    addEntryFn := (·.cons)
    addImportedFn := mkStateFromImportedEntries (·.cons) {}
  }

/-- Current annotation's location: `(pos "line:col", module string, line number)`. -/
private def refLoc : TacticM (String × String × Nat) := do
  let fileMap ← getFileMap
  let modName := (← getMainModule).toString
  return match (← getRef).getPos? with
    | some p => let lc := fileMap.toPosition p; (s!"{lc.line}:{lc.column}", modName, lc.line)
    | none   => ("?", modName, 0)

/-- `euclid_sentence "loc" "euclid text" (name : type) := by tac`

Realizes one Euclid sentence.  Elaborates to `have name : type := by tac` (identical proof
term / context to a plain `have`) and records a `logical` annotation into `faithfulExt`. -/
syntax (name := euclidSentence)
  "euclid_sentence " str str "(" ident " : " term ")" ":=" "by " tacticSeq : tactic

elab_rules : tactic
  | `(tactic| euclid_sentence $loc:str $txt:str ($nm:ident : $ty:term) := by $tac) => do
    let (posStr, modName, lineNo) ← refLoc
    -- Surface syntax of the type (verbatim slice when available).
    let typeStr := (ty.raw.reprint).getD (toString ty)
    modifyEnv fun env => faithfulExt.addEntry env {
      loc  := loc.getString
      text := txt.getString
      type := typeStr
      name := nm.getId.toString
      pos  := posStr
      mod  := modName
      line := lineNo
      kind := "logical" }
    -- Emit the real `have`; proof term and local context unchanged.
    evalTactic (← `(tactic| have $nm:ident : $ty := by $tac))

/-- `euclid_intro_sentence "loc" "euclid text"` and `euclid_conclude_sentence "loc" "euclid text"`

Record a *structural* Euclid sentence — the enunciation / "I say that" preamble (placed right
after `euclid_intros`) or the closing restatement + QED boilerplate (placed at the final step).
These contribute their text to the criterion-1 concatenation but are NOT logical steps: they emit
no `have` (the tactic is a `skip`), so the proof term and local context are unchanged. -/
syntax (name := euclidIntroSentence)
  "euclid_intro_sentence " str str : tactic
syntax (name := euclidConcludeSentence)
  "euclid_conclude_sentence " str str : tactic

/-- `euclid_wts "loc" "euclid text"`

Record a *structural* mid-proof "I say that …" (what-to-show) sentence. Like the intro/conclude
tactics it emits no `have` (proof term / context unchanged) and only contributes its text to the
criterion-1 concatenation — but unlike them it is permitted MID-proof. Euclid's "I say that X"
announces the goal; it is NOT an assertion that X is already proven, so it carries no claim. The real
content X is established by the following sentences and assembled by the trailing `exact`. -/
syntax (name := euclidWts)
  "euclid_wts " str str : tactic

/-- Shared recorder for the structural tactics. -/
private def recordStructural (loc txt : TSyntax `str) : TacticM Unit := do
  let (posStr, modName, lineNo) ← refLoc
  modifyEnv fun env => faithfulExt.addEntry env {
    loc  := loc.getString
    text := txt.getString
    type := ""
    name := ""
    pos  := posStr
    mod  := modName
    line := lineNo
    kind := "structural" }
  -- No tactic is emitted: this is a pure annotation, valid whether or not goals remain (it may
  -- follow the final `exact`). Recording only — proof term and local context are untouched.
  pure ()

elab_rules : tactic
  | `(tactic| euclid_intro_sentence $loc:str $txt:str)    => recordStructural loc txt
  | `(tactic| euclid_conclude_sentence $loc:str $txt:str) => recordStructural loc txt
  | `(tactic| euclid_wts $loc:str $txt:str)               => recordStructural loc txt

-- Faithfulness CHECKING (criterion 1: concatenate sentence texts, compare to the canonical
-- source) is done OUTSIDE Lean by `scripts/check_faithful.py`, which reads these annotations
-- from the source file. That keeps text-checking instant (no recompile / no SMT). This module
-- only RECORDS the annotations; the optional `lake exe` gate that reads them back from the
-- compiled .olean is deferred (see plan / todos).

/-- `euclid_assumption "euclid text" (tac)` — every wired hypothesis slot, in ONE fixed shape.

A string (documentary — Lean ignores it; the faithfulness checker reads it to confirm a reasoning
citation is a substring of its sentence) followed by a single **bracket-delimited** tactic that is the
actual proof. `wire_main.py` emits exactly:

    (by euclid_assumption "TEXT" (show T; assumption))     -- structural (TEXT = "") and plain reasoning
    (by euclid_assumption "TEXT" (show T; exact pf))       -- reasoning whose input is a conjunct projection

The brackets bound the proof unambiguously (so the recognizer's balanced-paren scan finds its end at any
depth, and Lean parses it as one parenthesized tactic); `show T` makes the slot's type visible and is
checked against the goal; the trailing tactic closes it from context. The text is `"`-free by
construction. There is no separate `use_override` syntax — an override is just `exact pf` inside the
brackets. -/
syntax (name := euclidAssumption)
  "euclid_assumption" str tactic : tactic

elab_rules : tactic
  | `(tactic| euclid_assumption $_:str $t:tactic) => evalTactic t

end SystemE.Tactics

syntax "euclid_finish" : tactic

elab "euclid_finish" : tactic => withMainContext <| EuclidFinish false

/-
  Invoked when `euclid_apply` has a hole to be filled.
  `hole` : The expression corresponding to the `Prop` to be filled
  `rule` : The whole argument of `euclid_apply`, e.g. `circle_from_points a b`
  `ident` : The identifier to be used if the `euclid_apply` instance is constructive
-/
private def EuclidSolve : EuclidStepM Unit := do
  pushHole
  EuclidFinish true
  finish

/-
  Main function for `euclid_apply`
-/
def EuclidApply (rule : Term) (idents : Array Ident)  : TacticM Unit := do
  if (← getGoals).length != 1 then
    throwError "euclid_apply only works when there is a single goal"
  let hnm ← getUnusedUserName `h
  let ruleExpr ← elabTerm rule none
  let τ ← inferType ruleExpr >>= instantiateMVars

  -- Faithfulness (criterion 3): record EVERY applied constant's COMPILER-RESOLVED fully-qualified
  -- name, module, and source line into `appliedExt` (no name filter). The name is already resolved
  -- by `elabTerm` above, so this adds no elaboration cost. We don't restrict to `proposition_*`/
  -- `helper_*` because `faithful_export` follows each recorded constant's TRANSITIVE dependency
  -- closure to find the `proposition_*` it (transitively) uses — so a prop cited inside ANY applied
  -- function (a `helper_<book>_step<n>`, or a function inside that function) still satisfies the
  -- citation. Pure-axiom constructions (`line_from_points`, `intersection_lines`) have empty
  -- closures, so recording them is harmless.
  if let .const declName _ := ruleExpr.getAppFn then
    let fileMap ← getFileMap
    let line := match (← getRef).getPos? with
      | some p => (fileMap.toPosition p).line
      | none   => 0
    let modName := (← getMainModule).toString
    modifyEnv fun env =>
      appliedExt.addEntry env { mod := modName, name := declName.toString, line := line }

  -- CLOSE-DIRECTLY FIRST (every shape EXCEPT `∃`): a fully-applied rule's conclusion may BE the
  -- current goal — a faithful `euclid_sentence` claim whose helper-conclusion == node-goal, for ANY
  -- shape: an atom, an `∧`/`∨`, a conditional `P → R` (C.N.1), or a universally-quantified conclusion
  -- `∀ x, …` (e.g. a uniqueness claim `¬∃ g, …` / `∀ g, g ≠ f → …`). `exact` closes it with ZERO SMT
  -- and no destructuring. The `first | …` wrapper gives full state-restoration on failure, so on
  -- failure (conclusion ≠ goal — the "add a fact to context" use) behavior is byte-identical to
  -- falling straight through to the shape-specific handling below. Citation recording (appliedExt)
  -- already ran above, so this loses nothing; on success we return early, skipping the destructuring
  -- AND the trailing `elimAllConjunctions` (a no-op once the goal is closed).
  -- We EXCLUDE `∃`: there the `as (x, …)` idents bind a witness that later lines reference, so closing
  -- the goal early would orphan those bindings. `∃` construction goals keep their exact old behavior.
  -- NOTE: faithful wires must carry NO trailing closer — a `(try split_ands) <;> assumption` trailer
  -- errors "no goals" once `exact` closes; wire_main regenerates wires trailer-free.
  let isExists := match τ.getAppFnArgs with
    | (``Exists, _) => true
    | _             => false
  if !isExists then
    let closedDirectly ← try
      evalTactic $ ← `(tactic| first | exact $rule)
      pure true
    catch _ =>
      pure false
    if closedDirectly then
      return ()

  match τ with
  | .forallE _ hole P _ => -- τ is an arrow
    if P.hasLooseBVars then  --  τ is an ∀ whose conclusion is NOT the goal → bind it into context
      evalTactic $ ← `(tactic| obtain ($(mkIdent hnm)) := $rule)
    else  -- τ is an implication whose consequent (not the implication itself) is the goal → EuclidSolve
      let Γ ← init (← getMainGoal) hole rule idents
      EuclidSolve |>.run Γ
  -- If there is no implication in the rule, i.e. no antecedent/hole to be filled, then just do the construction.
  | e =>
    match e.getAppFnArgs with
    | (``Exists, _) =>  -- τ is `∃ x, ...`
      let closedByExact ← try
        evalTactic $ ← `(tactic| exact $rule)
        pure true
      catch _ =>
        pure false
      if !closedByExact then
        evalTactic $ ← `(tactic| obtain ⟨$idents,*, ($(mkIdent hnm))⟩ := $rule)
    | _ =>
      evalTactic $ ← `(tactic| first
        | (obtain ⟨$(mkIdent hnm)⟩ := $rule)
        | (obtain $(mkIdent hnm) := $rule))

  elimAllConjunctions

syntax "euclid_apply" term : tactic

syntax "euclid_apply" term "as" ident : tactic

syntax "euclid_apply" term "as" "(" ident,+ ")" : tactic

syntax "euclid_assert" term : tactic

elab_rules : tactic
  | `(tactic| euclid_apply $t as $i) =>
    withMainContext $ EuclidApply t #[i]
  | `(tactic| euclid_apply $t as ($is,*)) =>
    withMainContext $ EuclidApply t is
  | `(tactic| euclid_apply $t) =>
    withMainContext $ EuclidApply t #[]

macro_rules
  | `(tactic| euclid_assert $t) => `(tactic| have : $t := by euclid_finish)

set_option systemE.trace false
set_option systemE.solverTime 300

end SystemE.Tactics

    (step3 : ∠ d:a:e = ∠ a:d:c) := by

        (by euclid_assumption "" (show a ≠ d; assumption))
        (by euclid_assumption "" (show e ≠ a; assumption)))

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""Faithfulness check (Design A) — pure text, no Lean, no SMT, instant.
3	
4	Checks two of the three `Book2/faithful.txt` criteria (the third — statement-faithfulness — is
5	human-checked):
6	
7	  CRITERION 1 (exact text recovery).  Concatenate the sentence texts in locator order and require
8	  the result to equal the canonical proposition source (`Book{N}/data/texts_proofs/{prop}.txt`)
9	  CHARACTER-FOR-CHARACTER (only tolerance: a trailing newline at EOF). Three annotation forms
10	  participate, joined by a single space:
11	      euclid_sentence          — a logical proof step (emits a `have`)
12	      euclid_intro_sentence    — STRUCTURAL: enunciation + "I say that …" (attaches to euclid_intros)
13	      euclid_conclude_sentence — STRUCTURAL: closing restatement + QED (attaches to the final `exact`)
14	
15	  CRITERION 3 (dependency reference, CONSTRUCTION-AWARE).  Every `[Prop.~B.N]` a sentence cites must be
16	  referenced by a `proposition_N` — as a CONSTRUCTION (`euclid_apply … as …` in Main, which may sit
17	  earlier than the citing sentence since objects are needed early) OR proof-internally (applied inside a
18	  step's helper). Satisfaction is WHOLE-MODULE, NOT block-scoped: source mode (number-only) checks the
19	  construction arm and DEFERS proof-internal cites to Phase B; olean mode (book-aware, transitive) checks
20	  both across the whole prop. This REFERENCES the dependency, it does not prove it is used — matching
21	  Euclid, who writes "by [Prop…]" without re-deriving.
22	
23	TWO MODES:
24	
25	  (default, source/regex — fast, offline, but NOT book-aware)
26	      python3 scripts/check_faithful.py "Book2/Prop01/Main.lean"
27	  Reads the annotations + `euclid_apply` lines straight from the .lean source. The criterion-3 check
28	  only matches the proposition NUMBER (`[Prop.~1.34]` is satisfied by any `proposition_34`); it does
29	  not authenticate the book B. Use for quick edits before a build.
30	
31	  (--olean — CERTAIN, book-aware)
32	      lake exe faithful_export Book2 > out.json
33	      python3 scripts/check_faithful.py --olean out.json
34	  Reads the JSON dumped from the compiled `.olean` by `faithful_export`. Texts are what the compiler
35	  elaborated; each cited `[Prop.~B.N]` is matched against the COMPILER-RESOLVED fully-qualified
36	  constant (e.g. `Elements.Book1.proposition_34'`), so the book is authenticated. Covers every
37	  proposition in the loaded module at once. This supersedes the source/regex stopgap.
38	
39	Neither mode verifies that the proof compiles — that is the *correctness* axis (`lake build`).
40	"""
41	import re, sys, os, json, io, contextlib
42	# Cone machinery (cone_names / propdir_of / prop_prefix) reused from the Phase-B lib so olean mode's
43	# notion of "the citing sentence's helper cone" is byte-identical to the number-only check.
44	import faithful_lib as fl
45	
46	# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
47	# Shared helpers
48	# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
49	
50	def norm(s: str) -> str:
51	    return " ".join(s.split())
52	
53	# A citation in Euclid's text, e.g. [Prop.~1.11]  →  (book, num) = ("1", "11").
54	CITE = re.compile(r'\[Prop\.~(\d+)\.(\d+)\]')
55	
56	# Bulk goal-closing tactics that must NOT appear in a faithful proof's MAIN body. A faithful proof
57	# closes its goal ONLY through the per-sentence `euclid_sentence` steps + their `euclid_apply`s (and
58	# `euclid_finish`/`euclid_intros`/`rw`/`exact`/`refine`/`constructor`). Any of these in the main file
59	# means the goal was likely cheat-closed by a leftover tactic from the old (unfaithful) proof, not by
60	# the faithful step chain. Only the proposition's MAIN file is linted; the per-sentence step files
61	# (`Book<N>/PropNN/stepN.lean`, theorem helper_<book>_stepN) are EXEMPT — scoped algebra is allowed in
62	# a step's own proof. Matched as whole words to avoid false hits inside identifiers.
63	FORBIDDEN_TACTICS = ["linarith", "nlinarith", "ring", "ring_nf", "simp", "omega",
64	                     "linear_combination", "norm_num", "field_simp", "polyrith"]
65	FORBIDDEN_RE = re.compile(r'(?<![\w.])(' + "|".join(FORBIDDEN_TACTICS) + r')(?![\w.])')
66	
67	def is_helper_file(path: str) -> bool:
68	    """A file is a STEP/helper file (exempt from the forbidden-tactic lint) unless it is a proposition
69	    MAIN file. New layout: `Book<N>/PropNN/Main.lean` is linted; `Book<N>/PropNN/stepN.lean` (and any
70	    other non-Main file in a prop folder) is exempt. Legacy flat layouts (`PropNN.lean`,
71	    `*_steps.lean`, `Scratch/`) are still handled for safety."""
72	    p = path.replace("\\", "/")
73	    base = p.rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
74	    if "/Scratch/" in p or p.startswith("Scratch/") or p.endswith("_steps.lean"):
75	        return True
76	    # In a per-prop folder (.../PropNN/<file>.lean), only Main.lean is the linted proposition file.
77	    if re.search(r"/Prop\d+/", p):
78	        return base != "Main.lean"
79	    return False
80	
81	def loc_key(loc: str):
82	    return [int(x) for x in loc.split(".") if x.isdigit()]
83	
84	def canon_path_for(book: str, prop: str):
85	    """Resolve the canonical proof text relative to LeanEuclidPlus/.
86	    Every book is foldered:  Book{N}/data/texts_proofs/{prop}.txt  (data/ holds the generated
87	    corpus). Book 1 is not special — the flat Book/ layout is gone."""

99	def report_dup_and_gap(items, ref_of) -> int:
100	    """items: list of dicts with 'loc'. ref_of(item) -> 'file:line' for messages. Returns 1 on
101	    duplicate or gap in the last locator segment, else 0."""
102	    locs = [it['loc'] for it in items]
103	    dups = sorted({l for l in locs if locs.count(l) > 1})
104	    if dups:
105	        for loc in dups:
106	            refs = [ref_of(it) for it in items if it['loc'] == loc]
107	            print(f"FAIL: duplicate locator {loc} at {','.join(refs)}")
108	        return 1
109	    keys = sorted(loc_key(l) for l in locs)
110	    last = [k[-1] for k in keys]
111	    if last and last == sorted(last):
112	        missing = [n for n in range(last[0], last[-1] + 1) if n not in last]
113	        if missing:
114	            stem = ".".join(map(str, keys[0][:-1]))
115	            print(f"FAIL: gap in locators — missing {', '.join(f'{stem}.{m}' for m in missing)}")
116	            return 1
117	    return 0

119	def criterion1_exact(items, canon_rel, canon_path):
120	    """items: list of dicts with 'loc','text','ref' (the right set for ONE prop), in any order.
121	    Concatenate in locator order, compare char-for-char to the canonical text.
122	    Returns (ok: bool, lines: list[str]) — caller prints. Does not print."""
123	    if not os.path.exists(canon_path):
124	        return False, [f"canonical source not found: {canon_rel}"]
125	    canon = open(canon_path, encoding="utf-8").read().rstrip("\n")
126	
127	    ordered = sorted(items, key=lambda it: loc_key(it['loc']))
128	    concat = " ".join(it['text'] for it in ordered)
129	    span = f"{len(ordered)} sentences ({ordered[0]['loc']}..{ordered[-1]['loc']}) vs {canon_rel}"
130	
131	    if concat == canon:
132	        return True, [f"concatenation reproduces canonical text exactly, in order ({span})"]
133	
134	    cw, mw = canon.split(), concat.split()
135	    for j in range(min(len(cw), len(mw))):
136	        if cw[j] != mw[j]:
137	            loc = ordered_loc_at(ordered, j)
138	            ref = next((it['ref'] for it in ordered if it['loc'] == loc), ordered[-1]['ref'])
139	            ctx = " ".join(mw[max(0, j-4):j])
140	            return False, [f"diverges at {loc} ({ref})",
141	                           f"  ...{ctx} <HERE>",
142	                           f"  canonical: {cw[j]!r}",
143	                           f"  your text: {mw[j]!r}"]
144	    if len(cw) == len(mw):
145	        # Same words in the same order, but the raw strings differ → a WHITESPACE mismatch: the source
146	        # has a multi-space run the single-space join didn't reproduce. Pinpoint it (still byte-exact to
147	        # PASS — this only makes the FAIL actionable so split/review can fix the boundary). See
148	        # faithful-split RULE 2: keep the extra space(s) inside a slice (trailing left / leading right).
149	        k = next((i for i in range(min(len(canon), len(concat))) if canon[i] != concat[i]),
150	                 min(len(canon), len(concat)))
151	        return False, ["whitespace mismatch — all words match, only spacing differs "
152	                       f"(first differs at char {k})",
153	                       f"  canonical: {canon[max(0, k-25):k+25]!r}",
154	                       f"  your text: {concat[max(0, k-25):k+25]!r}",
155	                       "  → the source has a multi-space run here; keep the extra space(s) INSIDE a "
156	                       "slice (trailing the left / leading the right) so the 1-space join reproduces it."]
157	    if len(mw) < len(cw):
158	        return False, [f"canonical text continues past your last sentence — "
159	                       f"missing (e.g.) {' '.join(cw[len(mw):len(mw)+8])!r} ..."]
160	    return False, [f"your text runs past the end of the canonical text: "
161	                   f"{' '.join(mw[len(cw):len(cw)+8])!r} ..."]

171	def ordered_loc_at(ordered, word_index):
172	    """Which sentence locator owns word number `word_index` in the concatenation."""
173	    i = 0
174	    for it in ordered:
175	        n = len(it['text'].split())
176	        if word_index < i + n:
177	            return it['loc']
178	        i += n
179	    return ordered[-1]['loc']

185	def strip_comments(src: str) -> str:
186	    """Blank out Lean `--` line and nested `/- … -/` block comments, REPLACING comment characters
187	    with spaces (newlines preserved) so byte offsets / line numbers are intact. String literals are
188	    passed through verbatim so a `--` INSIDE an annotation text (e.g. Euclid's "cut---equally") is
189	    not mistaken for a line comment."""
190	    out, i, n, depth = [], 0, len(src), 0
191	    while i < n:
192	        # A double-quoted string literal at top level (not inside a block comment) is copied as-is,
193	        # honoring Lean's `\"`/`\\` escapes, so embedded `--` / `/-` never reads as a comment.
194	        if depth == 0 and src[i] == '"':
195	            out.append(src[i]); i += 1
196	            while i < n:
197	                if src[i] == "\\" and i + 1 < n:
198	                    out.append(src[i]); out.append(src[i+1]); i += 2; continue
199	                out.append(src[i])
200	                if src[i] == '"':
201	                    i += 1; break
202	                i += 1
203	            continue
204	        two = src[i:i+2]
205	        if depth == 0 and two == "--":
206	            while i < n and src[i] != "\n":
207	                out.append(" "); i += 1
208	            continue
209	        if two == "/-":
210	            depth += 1; out.append("  "); i += 2; continue
211	        if two == "-/" and depth > 0:
212	            depth -= 1; out.append("  "); i += 2; continue
213	        if depth > 0:
214	            out.append("\n" if src[i] == "\n" else " "); i += 1; continue
215	        out.append(src[i]); i += 1
216	    return "".join(out)

220	#  but placement-unconstrained — so the True-gate skips it, the intro/conclude placement gate ignores
221	#  it, and only its text tiles.)
222	PAT = re.compile(
223	    r'euclid_(sentence|intro_sentence|conclude_sentence|wts)\s*'
224	    r'"((?:[^"\\]|\\.)*)"\s*"((?:[^"\\]|\\.)*)"')

226	def sentence_claim(src: str, start_pos: int):
227	    """Given `src` (comment-stripped) and a position at/after an `euclid_sentence`'s text string,
228	    return the claim type inside the following `(ident : CLAIM) :=`, whitespace-normalized, or None.
229	    Balances parens so nested `()` in the claim are handled. ONLY meaningful for `euclid_sentence`
230	    (intro/conclude sentences carry no `(name : claim)` binder)."""
231	    i = src.find("(", start_pos)
232	    if i < 0:
233	        return None
234	    depth, j = 0, i
235	    while j < len(src):
236	        if src[j] == "(":
237	            depth += 1
238	        elif src[j] == ")":
239	            depth -= 1
240	            if depth == 0:
241	                break
242	        j += 1
243	    else:
244	        return None
245	    m = re.match(r'\s*\w+\s*:\s*(.*)$', src[i + 1:j], re.DOTALL)   # "ident : CLAIM"
246	    return " ".join(m.group(1).split()) if m else None

493	            # granularity differs (book-aware here, number-only there). The export's per-`euclid_apply`
494	            # `appliedExt` record (the `applied` array, keyed by module) is the reliable source: the `deps`
495	            # transitive closure is empty for SMT-discharged applies (the prop never lands in the term), but
496	            # IS populated for direct term-level calls — so the deps fallback (below) catches those.
497	            # Criterion 3 is a REFERENCE check (Euclid writes "by [Prop X]").
498	            main_mod = sents[0]['mod']
499	            propdir = None
500	            if main_mod.endswith(".Main"):
501	                try:                                                      # Book2.Prop05.Main -> Book2/Prop05
502	                    propdir = fl.propdir_of(main_mod[:-len(".Main")].replace(".", os.sep))
503	                except fl.FaithfulError:
504	                    propdir = None                                        # no folder on disk → construction arm only
505	            mod_prefix = fl.prop_prefix(propdir) if propdir else None     # e.g. "Book2.Prop05"
506	            # locator → node name (authoritative map from the parsed `have`/sentence tree, not a name guess).
507	            try:
508	                occ = fl.parse_occurrences(propdir) if propdir else {}
509	            except fl.FaithfulError:
510	                occ = {}
511	            node_by_loc = {nd.loc: nm for nm, nds in occ.items() for nd in nds
512	                           if nd.kind == "sentence" and nd.loc is not None}
513	            try:                                                          # @suppress_deps_check waivers (loc → reason)
514	                suppressed = fl.suppressed_dep_locs(propdir) if propdir else {}
515	            except fl.FaithfulError as e:
516	                suppressed = {}
517	                group_rc |= report("every @suppress_deps_check tag is well-formed", False, [str(e)])
518	            construction = applied_by_mod.get(main_mod, [])               # whole-Main `as` constructions
519	            dep_lines, waived, n_cites = [], [], 0
520	            for s in sents:
521	                if s.get('kind') == 'structural':
522	                    continue                                              # intro/conclude/wts: background citations, not proof steps
523	                if s['loc'] in suppressed:                                # criterion-3 waived (documented reason)
524	                    waived.append(f"{s['loc']}: {suppressed[s['loc']]}")
525	                    continue
526	                for cbook, num in CITE.findall(s['text']):
527	                    n_cites += 1
528	                    if any(name_matches(ap['name'], cbook, num) for ap in construction):
529	                        continue                                          # construction arm
530	                    # proof arm: search the citing sentence's cone modules (if it has a node + we found the dir).
531	                    cone_hit = False
532	                    node = node_by_loc.get(s['loc'])
533	                    if node is not None and propdir is not None:
534	                        try:
535	                            cone = fl.cone_names(propdir, node)
536	                        except fl.FaithfulError:
537	                            cone = set()
538	                        cone_mods = {f"{mod_prefix}.{n}" for n in cone}
539	                        cone_hit = any(name_matches(ap['name'], cbook, num)
540	                                       for m in cone_mods for ap in applied_by_mod.get(m, []))
541	                        if not cone_hit and cone:
542	                            # Fallback: check transitive deps of Main-applied helpers whose name
543	                            # corresponds to a cone node. Catches direct term-level proposition calls
544	                            # inside a helper (not via euclid_apply) — the prop appears in the
545	                            # propClosure deps attached to the Main apply entry, not in the step module's
546	                            # applied_by_mod, so the direct check above misses it.
547	                            pfx = f"helper_{book}_{prop}_"
548	                            for ap in applied_by_mod.get(main_mod, []):
549	                                local = ap['name'].rsplit('.', 1)[-1] if '.' in ap['name'] else ap['name']
550	                                if local.startswith(pfx) and local[len(pfx):] in cone:
551	                                    if any(name_matches(dep, cbook, num) for dep in ap.get('deps', [])):
552	                                        cone_hit = True
553	                                        break
554	                    if cone_hit:
555	                        continue
556	                    where = f"its helper cone (node `{node}`)" if node else \
557	                            "any helper cone (structural sentence — must be a Main construction)"
558	                    dep_lines.append(f"{s['loc']} ({s['ref']}) cites [Prop.~{cbook}.{num}] but no "
559	                                     f"`proposition_{num}` of Book {cbook} is applied `… as …` in {main_mod} "
560	                                     f"(construction) nor inside {where}")
561	            ok_lines = dep_lines or [f"all {n_cites} citation(s) resolve to the cited book+number"]
562	            if waived:
563	                ok_lines = ok_lines + [f"{len(waived)} sentence(s) waived by @suppress_deps_check:"] \
564	                           + [f"    {w}" for w in waived]
565	            group_rc |= report("every cited [Prop.~B.M] is referenced in the prop (book-aware: Main construction or sentence's cone)",
566	                         not dep_lines, ok_lines)
567	
568	            canon_rel, canon_path = canon_path_for(book, prop)
569	            ok1, lines1 = criterion1_exact(sents, canon_rel, canon_path)
570	            group_rc |= report("all sentences present + concatenation reproduces the original text exactly",
571	                         ok1, lines1)
572	
573	        rc |= group_rc
574	        if not is_focus:
575	            if group_rc != 0:
576	                if buf is not None:
577	                    sys.stdout.write(buf.getvalue())
578	                bg_fails.append(f"Book{book} Prop {prop}")
579	            else:
580	                bg_pass += 1
581	
582	    if focus is not None:
583	        if bg_fails:
584	            print(f"  [WARN] {len(bg_fails)} background prop(s) also FAILED: {', '.join(bg_fails)}")
585	        elif bg_pass > 0:
586	            print(f"  [also checked {bg_pass} background prop(s): all pass]")
587	    # Reminder: that each step's TYPE honestly captures its sentence is HUMAN-checked — not here.
588	    print("  [note] not machine-checked: that each step's type honestly captures its sentence (review by hand)")
589	    print(f"  => {'ALL PASS' if rc == 0 else 'FAILED'} (--olean mode, authoritative)")
590	    return rc
591	
592	# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
593	
594	def check_split(propdir: str) -> int:
595	    """--split mode (Phase-A stage-1 gate): verify Book<N>/PropNN/split.json TILES the canonical text
596	    byte-for-byte BEFORE translate/assemble is paid for. Reuses criterion1_exact, so a whitespace-only
597	    miss gets the same actionable "char N" diagnostic. Reads split.json + the canonical .txt; and, on
598	    deduction entries carrying the OPT-IN "spans" field, checks the assertion/assumption/glue spans
599	    reconstruct the sentence char-for-char (and warns on a compound assertion span).
600	    Run this right after faithful-split and fix the slices until it PASSES."""
601	    base = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))       # LeanEuclidPlus/
602	    pd = propdir if os.path.isabs(propdir) else os.path.join(base, propdir)
603	    sp = os.path.join(pd, "split.json")
604	    print(f"=== --split — {propdir.rstrip('/')}/split.json vs canonical ===")
605	    m = re.search(r'Book(\d+)[/\\]+Prop0*(\d+)', propdir)
606	    if not m:
607	        print(f"  [FAIL] cannot parse Book<N>/Prop<NN> from: {propdir}")
608	        return 1
609	    book, prop = m.group(1), m.group(2)
610	    if not os.path.exists(sp):
611	        print(f"  [FAIL] split.json not found: {os.path.relpath(sp, base)}")
612	        return 1
613	    try:
614	        data = json.load(open(sp, encoding="utf-8"))
615	    except ValueError as e:
616	        print(f"  [FAIL] split.json is not valid JSON: {e}")
617	        return 1
618	    if not isinstance(data, list) or not data:
619	        print("  [FAIL] split.json must be a non-empty JSON array")
620	        return 1
621	    # INDEX = array position (auto — the split agent never writes it); the array is already in order.
622	    items = [{'loc': f"{book}.{prop}.{i}", 'text': e.get('text', ''),
623	              'ref': f"split.json[{i}]"} for i, e in enumerate(data)]
624	    canon_rel, canon_path = canon_path_for(book, prop)
625	    ok, lines = criterion1_exact(items, canon_rel, canon_path)
626	    rc = report("split.json tiles the canonical text byte-for-byte (whitespace included)", ok, lines)
627	
628	    # OPT-IN assertion/assumption discipline: only entries carrying a "spans" field are checked, so
629	    # legacy split.json (no spans) is completely unaffected. Each span is {"label": assertion|assumption|
630	    # glue, "text": <verbatim slice>}. (a) HARD: the spans must reconstruct the sentence CHARACTER-FOR-
631	    # CHARACTER (empty join — no separator — every weird/double/trailing space included). (b) WARN: an
632	    # `assertion` span with a comma or " and " is likely a compound claim to split (the AI decides).
633	    concat_fails, warn_lines = [], []
634	    for i, e in enumerate(data):
635	        if not isinstance(e, dict) or not e.get("spans"):
636	            continue
637	        spans, ref, txt = e["spans"], f"split.json[{i}]", e.get("text", "")
638	        joined = "".join(sp.get("text", "") for sp in spans if isinstance(sp, dict))
639	        if joined != txt:
640	            k = next((c for c in range(min(len(joined), len(txt))) if joined[c] != txt[c]),
641	                     min(len(joined), len(txt)))
642	            concat_fails += [f"{ref}: spans do not reconstruct the sentence (first differ at char {k})",
643	                             f"    text : {txt[max(0, k - 20):k + 20]!r}",
644	                             f"    spans: {joined[max(0, k - 20):k + 20]!r}"]
645	        for sp in spans:
646	            if isinstance(sp, dict) and sp.get("label") == "assertion":
647	                a = sp.get("text", "")
648	                if "," in a or " and " in norm(a):
649	                    warn_lines.append(f"{ref} assertion span may be COMPOUND (has ',' or ' and '): {norm(a)!r}")
650	    rc |= report("deduction spans reconstruct their sentence char-for-char (opt-in)",
651	                 not concat_fails,
652	                 concat_fails or ["no `spans` fields present, or all reconstruct exactly"])
653	    for w in warn_lines:
654	        print(f"  [warn] {w}")
655	        print( "         → likely two claims; split into atomic entries (AI makes the final call)")
656	
657	    # REDUCTIO FRAMES (opt-in): entries carrying a `frame` object drive the assembler's nested
658	    # `have habsurd … := by intro …` skeleton. They must form well-formed triples, LINKED BY TEXT (no
659	    # indices): a `reductio_close`'s `closes` copies its `reductio_open`'s `supposition` VERBATIM, with a
660	    # `contradiction` sitting between them. This catches a malformed reductio at split time — before the
661	    # assembler stamps a broken block. (`wts` role + a frame-free split are completely unaffected.)
662	    frames = [(i, e["frame"]) for i, e in enumerate(data)
663	              if isinstance(e, dict) and isinstance(e.get("frame"), dict) and e["frame"].get("kind")]
664	    frame_problems = []
665	    if frames:
666	        KNOWN = {"reductio_open", "contradiction", "reductio_close"}
667	        opens  = [(i, fr.get("supposition")) for i, fr in frames if fr["kind"] == "reductio_open"]
668	        closes = [(i, fr.get("closes"))      for i, fr in frames if fr["kind"] == "reductio_close"]
669	        contras = [i for i, fr in frames if fr["kind"] == "contradiction"]
670	        for i, fr in frames:
671	            if fr["kind"] not in KNOWN:
672	                frame_problems.append(f"split.json[{i}]: unknown frame kind {fr['kind']!r} (expected "
673	                                      "reductio_open / contradiction / reductio_close)")
674	        for i, supp in opens:
675	            if not supp:
676	                frame_problems.append(f"split.json[{i}]: reductio_open has no `supposition` text")
677	                continue
678	            match = [j for j, c in closes if c and norm(c) == norm(supp)]
679	            if not match:
680	                frame_problems.append(f"split.json[{i}]: reductio_open supposition {norm(supp)!r} has no "
681	                                      "matching reductio_close (a close's `closes` must copy it verbatim)")
682	                continue
683	            j = match[0]
684	            if j < i:
685	                frame_problems.append(f"split.json[{i}]: its reductio_close at [{j}] precedes the open")
686	            elif not any(i < k < j for k in contras):
687	                frame_problems.append(f"split.json[{i}]: no `contradiction` frame between the open and its "
688	                                      f"close at [{j}]")
689	        for j, c in closes:
690	            if not c:
691	                frame_problems.append(f"split.json[{j}]: reductio_close has no `closes` text")
692	            elif not any(s and norm(s) == norm(c) for _, s in opens):
693	                frame_problems.append(f"split.json[{j}]: reductio_close `closes` {norm(c)!r} matches no "
694	                                      "reductio_open `supposition`")
695	        if contras and not opens:
696	            frame_problems.append("a `contradiction` frame is present but no `reductio_open` opens it")
697	        rc |= report("reductio frames form well-formed open/contradiction/close triples (linked by text)",
698	                     not frame_problems, frame_problems or [f"{len(opens)} reductio(s) well-formed"])
699	
700	    print(f"  => {'PASS' if rc == 0 else 'FAILED'} (--split mode)")
701	    return rc
702	
703	def main(argv) -> int:
704	    global RELAXED
705	    if "--relaxed" in argv:
706	        RELAXED = True
707	        argv = [a for a in argv if a != "--relaxed"]
708	    if len(argv) >= 2 and argv[0] == "--olean":
709	        json_path = argv[1]
710	        focus = None
711	        if len(argv) == 4 and argv[2] == "--focus":
712	            m = re.search(r'Book(\d+)\.Prop0*(\d+)', argv[3])
713	            if m:
714	                focus = (m.group(1), m.group(2))
715	        return check_olean(json_path, focus=focus)
716	    if len(argv) == 2 and argv[0] == "--split":
717	        return check_split(argv[1])
718	    if len(argv) == 1 and not argv[0].startswith("--"):
719	        return check_source(argv[0])
720	    print(__doc__)
721	    return 2
722	
723	if __name__ == "__main__":
724	    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))
